goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: raw_html cook method renders raw feed content with no sanitization and best.html.erb outputs it via raw post.cooked, enabling stored XSS in the same-origin embed iframe

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a `:raw_html` cook method in `Post#cook` that returns `raw` directly (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and passes in `contents` derived from RSS (`i.content`) after `CGI.unescapeHTML(...)`, with no HTML sanitization. The embed UI then renders this content with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, which will execute any embedded script/handler attributes stored in the post. This is a stored XSS vector in the Discourse-origin embed iframe (and potentially anywhere else that displays `post.cooked` for these posts).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration sets cook_method column default to 1 (raw_html), bypassing the cooking pipeline for all new posts

adjudication.rationale: The migration `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` sets the default to `1`, but `Post.cook_methods` is defined as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`. In Discourse, these enums are 1-based (e.g., existing `Post.types` uses the same pattern), so `1` corresponds to `:regular`, not `:raw_html`. The code also only bypasses cooking when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, so the default does not bypass the pipeline for new posts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js uses substring match discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1, so origins containing the target URL string (e.g. https://discourse.example.com.attacker.com/) pass the check and can set arbitrary iframe height
url and feed title/content interpolated unescaped into HTML strings in topic_embed.rb, allowing attribute breakout and markup injection via crafted feed entries

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends an HTML snippet to `contents` using direct string interpolation: `"#{url}"` inside `I18n.t(...)`. The only check on `url` is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes, spaces, or other characters that can break out of the `href` attribute (e.g., `http://x' onclick='...`). That creates verifiable markup/attribute injection. Additionally, the feed-provided `contents` is treated as raw HTML for posts (`cook_method: :raw_html` causes `Post#cook` to return `raw`), and the embed view renders it with `raw post.cooked`, so unsanitized feed HTML (from `PollFeed`, which uses `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` but does not sanitize tags/attributes) can be injected directly into rendered pages.

The candidate doesn’t mention the `description` fallback explicitly but flags the same root cause.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No rescue around open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) in poll_feed.rb, so network errors kill the job with retry: false

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` after `require 'open-uri'` with no error handling. `open(...)` can raise (e.g., timeouts, DNS, HTTP errors), which would cause `execute` to raise and the Sidekiq job to fail. Since the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, Sidekiq will not retry on such transient failures, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import does find-then-create with no locking, so concurrent retrievals raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique on the unique embed_url index and can leave orphan topics

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, proceeds to create a new topic/post and then `TopicEmbed.create!(embed_url: url, ...)`. There is a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, and there is no locking or upsert, so two concurrent imports for the same URL can both observe `embed.blank?` and then race; the loser will raise an `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (or equivalent) on `create!`, causing the job/request to error. However, the creation is wrapped in `Topic.transaction do ... end`, so if the `create!` fails the transaction should roll back the topic/post as well, making the “leave orphan topics” part not clearly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: retrieve_topic.rb uses the viewing user's staff status to decide throttling (no_throttle), disabling the throttle for everyone when any staff member hits the page

adjudication.rationale: In `retrieve_topic.rb`, the job passes `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` to `TopicRetriever`, where `retrieved_recently?` skips throttling only when `@opts[:no_throttle]` is truthy. That bypass applies only to that specific job/request created for a staff `current_user` (`Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), ...)`). It does not “disable the throttle for everyone” globally; non-staff requests still run the normal Redis-based throttling. While staff bypass means the Redis throttle key is not set by staff requests, other users are not automatically unthrottled by that.

adjudication_records.issue_text: loading.html.erb reloads unconditionally every 30 seconds forever, generating continuous load and repeated job enqueues if the retrieve job fails

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` the script calls `document.location.reload()` every 30 seconds with no stop condition. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil it enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. So every reload triggers another request that will re-enqueue `retrieve_topic` again as long as the embed isn't created (e.g., if retrieval keeps failing or is blocked). While `TopicRetriever` throttles actual retrieval to once per 60 seconds, the controller still enqueues a new job per reload/request, and the repeated reloads also generate continuous HTTP load.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import thor task removed the --category option and created_at preservation, so imported topics land in the default category and lose original timestamps

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the diff removes `method_option :category` and the code that looked up `category_id` and passed `category: category_id` into `PostCreator`. It also replaces `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) ...)` with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`.import` ultimately call `PostCreator.new` without `created_at` or `category`, so Disqus imports will no longer preserve original timestamps and cannot target a specified category (thus defaulting to whatever the default category behavior is).

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls drops the port for explicit default ports with non-matching scheme (http://host:443, https://host:80) and ignores protocol-relative and fragment/query-only relative URLs, leaving links broken

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, the port is only preserved when it is neither 80 nor 443:

```rb
prefix << ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443
```

This incorrectly drops an explicit non-default port when it happens to be 443 on an http URL (http://host:443/...) or 80 on an https URL (https://host:80/...), producing a different origin than the source URL.

Also, URL rewriting only occurs when href/src starts with '/':

```rb
if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')
```

So other common “relative” forms (e.g. "page.html", "../img.png", "?q=1", "#frag") are left untouched and will resolve relative to the Discourse embed page rather than the source article, which can break links or point them to the wrong place. Protocol-relative URLs ("//cdn...") are also not handled, leaving them scheme-relative to Discourse rather than the original URL’s scheme.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously re-parses the entire feed on every embed request instead of scheduling it, potentially revising hundreds of unrelated topics

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, it directly calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` (synchronous, not enqueued) before falling back to `fetch_http`. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` then parses the entire feed (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`) and iterates `rss.items.each`, calling `TopicEmbed.import` for every item, which can create/update posts/topics unrelated to the requested `@embed_url`. This path can be reached from an embed request that triggers `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and then `TopicRetriever#retrieve`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed_spec.rb asserts post.cooked.start_with?(...) which passes even if extra content is appended; no spec covers XSS in imported content or the raw_html default column value

adjudication.rationale: The finding mainly critiques test coverage/strength rather than identifying a defect introduced by the diff. In `topic_embed_spec.rb`, using `start_with?` is intentional for verifying URL absolutization at the beginning of the cooked HTML; the imported post is expected to potentially include additional HTML (e.g., the appended “Imported from” footer), so “extra content appended” does not indicate a bug. The note about “no spec covers XSS” is true as a coverage gap, but it’s not a verifiable problem in the diff by itself. Finally, the migration sets `posts.cook_method` default to `1`, and the enum is defined as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`, which in this codebase conventionally maps `:regular` to `1`, so there is no demonstrated incorrect default to flag here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: content_sha1 is computed from pre-absolutize_urls content while the stored post contains absolutized content, causing sha mismatches and spurious revisions when URL scheme/port changes

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, `content_sha1` is consistently computed from the pre-`absolutize_urls` `contents` and stored in `topic_embeds.content_sha1`. On subsequent imports it is recomputed from the same kind of pre-absolutized `contents` and compared only against the stored `topic_embeds.content_sha1`—it is never compared against the post’s stored (absolutized) `raw`/`cooked`. Therefore there is no SHA mismatch caused by `absolutize_urls` alone. Also, a URL scheme/port change would change `embed_url`, and since the lookup is `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` with a unique index on `embed_url`, that would create a new embed rather than spuriously revising an existing one.
